title: QBR - Zephyr Labs - Health Check
summary: Quarterly health check covering usage trends, cost drivers, recent reliability incidents, upcoming roadmap items and contract renewal discussions. Agreed to run a latency benchmark for Zephyr's main inference route, share updated pricing for dedicated capacity, and schedule a security deep-dive for SSO/KMS integration.
next_steps: Redwood to send updated Dedicated pricing and commitment options by 2025-07-25
SE to run latency + P95 benchmark on customer's test route and share results by 2025-07-30
Schedule security deep-dive (SSO/KMS/audit logs) for week of 2025-08-04

Liam O'Neill - Run latency benchmark and provide raw metrics + alpha config used - Due: 2025-07-30
Emma Chen - Send Dedicated pricing sheet and contract options - Due: 2025-07-25

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-07-22 16:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Emma Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Zephyr Head of ML), Carlos Rodriguez (Zephyr CTO), Daniel Park (Zephyr Finance Ops)

Summary (auto): QBR covering usage/costs, reliability incidents in June, options for Dedicated capacity, and roadmap asks. Next steps captured.

[00:00] Emma Chen: All right, hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Emma from Redwood. We think we have about 45 minutes. Ravi and Liam are with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Maya Singh: Good thanks, busy week but excited to walk through the QBR.
[00:14] Carlos Rodriguez: Morning all, quick note, Daniel's joining for the cost bits.
[00:18] Daniel Park: Yep here — should be about 20 minutes on finance details.
[00:22] Ravi Patel: Great, we'll kick off with usage trends and then hand to Liam for reliability and then open for roadmap questions.

[02:05] Ravi Patel: So first slide, total tokens this quarter up about 42% q/q, embeddings steady at ~10M per month. The big driver was the new customer-facing assistant we launched in May. Cost per token has drifted up slightly because of higher p95 lengths, and we can see KV cache hit rates are around 62% on average which is below our recommended 75%.
[02:46] Maya Singh: Right, we saw that. The assistant prompts are longer, and we do some multi-pass reranking which increases tokens. Would caching help with the multi turn?
[02:58] Liam O'Neill: Yeah caching helps for prefixes and repeated context. We recommended increasing prefix canonicalization and moving some of the rerank stage to embeddings-only scoring to cut token regeneration. There's also quantization options to drop inference cost with minimal quality loss.
[03:22] Maya Singh: Is that something we can test in a POC?
[03:26] Liam O'Neill: Absolutely — we can run a pilot with quantized model variants and measure latency and quality delta.

[05:00] Daniel Park: On costs, the monthly bill jumped ~18% month-over-month. We're looking at options: keep hosted for agility vs commit to Dedicated for predictable unit costs. What break-even look like?
[05:18] Ravi Patel: Based on current usage, Dedicated starts to make sense at your current sustained throughput — rough back of envelope shows 6-9 months payback if you commit to 1 GPU pool for the heaviest route. But we should run a more precise model and include burst pricing and autoscale overheads.
[05:40] Daniel Park: Can you put that model in the one-pager?
[05:42] Emma Chen: Yes, we'll include a detailed cost comparison and scenarios.

[07:10] Liam O'Neill: Quick note on reliability — in June there were two incidents affecting the us-west region: a 12-minute elevated latency window due to kernel-level scheduling bug on a third-party runtime, and a 27-minute P95 spike during a traffic surge. Both had fallbacks to smaller model variants but one customer route saw degraded quality. Since then we've rolled kernel patch and increased autoscaler headroom.
[07:42] Carlos Rodriguez: For that P95 spike, did Redwood's fallback kick in automatically? We saw some user complaints about hallucination rates.
[07:51] Liam O'Neill: The fallback executed but the fallback model was unoptimized for that prompt family — so quality dipped. We've added a new policy to prefer compatible model variant mapping per route and are rolling a change to test-canary the variant before global fallback.
[08:10] Maya Singh: Can you share the incident postmortem and the tracing for our route?
[08:15] Liam O'Neill: We'll share the incident postmortem and the route traces — expect that in the ticket.

[10:00] Ravi Patel: On SLAs and observability, we saw upticks in error rates during the incident but overall uptime is still 99.95% for the quarter. You asked about audit logs and retention — Redwood can extend retention for enterprise bundles and integrate with your SIEM exports.
[10:21] Carlos Rodriguez: We need 12-month logs forwarded to our LogStore for compliance. Is that supported?
[10:26] Emma Chen: Yes, that's a supported add-on. We'll include configuration with the security deep-dive.

[12:30] Maya Singh: On model roadmap: we're interested in lower-latency small context models for realtime chat, more deterministic tokenization (to reduce hallucination), and better version pinning for canary. Any updates from Redwood?
[12:45] Liam O'Neill: Roadmap-wise, we have early access for faster compilation kernels for short-seq workloads, a canary rollout UI improvement, and a new cache analytics page that breaks down prefix hit% by route. We also plan to add model-variant compatibility metadata to avoid the fallback quality issue.

[15:00] Daniel Park: Regarding data residency and encryption — our legal needs SSO and KMS with customer-managed keys for any Dedicated deployment. What's the path there?
[15:14] Emma Chen: For Dedicated and Private we support integration with your KMS/HSM and SAML SSO; for Dedicated we can enable customer-managed KMS and provide audit logs. For Private we offer the on-prem option if required for air-gapped.
[15:32] Carlos Rodriguez: Great. Can we get a security questionnaire and architecture diagram?
[15:35] Ravi Patel: Yes, we'll send the security pack and propose a security deep-dive meeting next week.

[18:20] Maya Singh: On the pilot you mentioned for quantization and caching — what metrics will you track?
[18:27] Liam O'Neill: We'll track latency P50/P95/P99, token cost per request, quality delta via your golden prompts, and cache hit ratios. We'll also provide a recommended configuration: batching window, KV cache TTLs, and a fallback mapping.
[18:44] Maya Singh: For the golden prompts, we'll push the top 20 later today.

[21:00] Daniel Park: Contract timeline — renewal in October. If we move to Dedicated, we might want a 12-month commit. Are there flexible tiers?
[21:13] Emma Chen: Yes, we have monthly and annual commit options. We'll include a few commitment tiers in the pricing sheet and show estimated savings and break-even.

[24:00] Carlos Rodriguez: A couple of quick technical asks — can we get per-token cost broken out by model and route? And can we export traces at token level?
[24:13] Ravi Patel: Per-token cost by model + route is available in the console; we'll export the breakdown for you. Token-level tracing is available via sampling; for full traces we recommend the trace-forward export to your observability cluster.

[27:40] Emma Chen: Let's walk through the proposed next steps — send the Dedicated pricing and one-pager, SE to run benchmark, security deep-dive. Anything to add?
[27:53] Maya Singh: Please include an estimate of quality impact for quantized variants.
[27:58] Liam O'Neill: We'll include measured ROUGE/BLEU-style metrics on your golden prompts and subjective pass/fail heatmap.

[30:10] (brief cross-talk, background noise)

[31:05] Daniel Park: On billing, can we set up a monthly threshold alert to notify finance before we hit unexpected surges?
[31:12] Emma Chen: Yes, we have budget alerts and rate limits. We'll propose thresholds and set up a shared billing dashboard read-only for your team.

[33:50] Maya Singh: One last thing — we are experimenting with a new customer-facing quick reply where latency must be <120ms p95. Do you think Dedicated can meet that?
[34:02] Liam O'Neill: For short sequence with optimized kernels and local model variants, Dedicated on the right GPU profile with warm KV cache should meet sub-120ms p95 for many routes, but we should run a targeted benchmark using your prompts and traffic profile. That's part of the action item.

[37:10] Carlos Rodriguez: Also curious about multi-region failover. If us-west has a problem, can we fail to eu-central with minimal cold-start?
[37:20] Liam O'Neill: We support cross-region routing with warm replicas and pre-warmed caches; it requires replication of KV caches and possibly model sharding depending on size. We'll outline options in the post-call doc.

[40:00] Ravi Patel: Recap: 1) Pricing + Dedicated options; 2) Latency benchmark + quantization pilot; 3) Security deep-dive; 4) Export of incident postmortem and traces; 5) Billing alerts & dashboard.

[41:30] Maya Singh: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

[41:34] Daniel Park: Thanks, appreciate the clear next steps.

[41:38] Emma Chen: We'll follow up with the one-pager and calendar invites.

[42:00] (meeting ends, 42:05)

Notes on transcription: Minor ASR artifacts — some product names rendered oddly (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache") and a few speaker mis-attributions in the auto transcript.
